pageCache.pageTitle: Sutton Courtenay CofE Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Love life; love learning; love one another
Welcome to our website!
At Sutton Courtenay, every child is valued for their uniqueness and placed at the heart of all we do.
Our warm, professional team builds strong relationships so every child can flourish in a safe and supportive environment.
Our core values—Ready, Respectful, Responsible—guide everything we do. Inspired by Matthew 7:25, we provide strong foundations for life and learning through our three pillars: Teaching & Learning, Curriculum, and Ethos & Culture, rooted in ambition, compassion and inclusivity.
We encourage children to Love life; love learning; love one another, helping them grow into wise, caring individuals who lead by example and make a difference in their communities.
Safeguarding is central to our work. We are committed to ensuring every child feels safe, valued, and empowered to achieve their best.
As part of Ridgeway Education Trust and in close partnership with All Saints Church, we celebrate our Christian distinctiveness while welcoming all. Our dedication to serving the community ensures that our school is a place of connection, support, and shared growth.
Together, we create a school where every child can thrive.

Governors
Multi Academy Trust and Local Governing Body
Sutton Courtenay Church of England Primary School joined the Ridgeway Education Trust (RET) on 1 April 2019 and joined Didcot Girls' School and St Birinus in the Multi Academy Trust (MAT).
Ridgeway Education Trust is run by a Board of Directors which has ultimate responsibility for running each academy within its structure and for setting the vision for schools within the MAT. You can find out more about Governance in the Trust by clicking this link. Each school retains its own Local Governing Body which includes representatives from staff, parents and members of the local community appointed for their particular skills and experience. Directors and Governors are appointed for a term of four years.
The Local Governing Body meets as a whole at least six times a year. You can find key documents below.
The RET Governance Officer is Rachel Harper rharper@ridgewayeducation.com
The Local Governing Body comprises:

pageCache.pageTitle: Sutton Courtenay CofE Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
I am proud to lead such a vibrant and ambitious school community here in the historical village of Sutton Courtenay. Our vision is clear: to empower every child to thrive, achieve, and grow into confident, compassionate individuals ready for the future.
At Sutton Courtenay CofE Primary School, our ethos shapes everything we do. We call it “The Way We Do Things Here”—a culture built on compassion, inclusion, and ambition. It means working together as staff, pupils, and families to create an environment where every child feels valued, challenged, and supported.
Our curriculum is rooted in research and strong foundations, designed to build deep knowledge and skills from Nursery through Year 6. Every subject has a clear purpose and progression, ensuring learning is meaningful and ambitious. We set high expectations and encourage children to work hard, take pride in their achievements, and develop resilience along the way.
Education here goes beyond academics. We offer rich cultural experiences and a strong focus on wellbeing and personal development, ensuring every child grows not only in knowledge but in character.
Our dedicated staff share a passion for lifelong learning and continually develop their expertise to deliver the very best for our pupils. Together, we create a dynamic, values-led environment where ambition and care shape everything we do—and where every child receives the world-class education they deserve.
We warmly invite you to explore our website and visit us in person. Please contact our office team at office@sutton-courtenay.school to arrange a visit.
I look forward to welcoming you to Sutton Courtenay CofE Primary School.
I believe that if we do our jobs well, the children of Sutton Courtenay CofE Primary School will grow into confident, compassionate leaders—ready to shape the future with knowledge, integrity, and ambition.
Raluca Chende Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Sutton Courtenay CofE Primary School - Nursery Admissions
pageCache.text:
Nursery Admissions
Nursery Class
If you are interested in your child joining our Nursery, please do make an appointment by contacting our school office on 01235 848 333 to arrange a visit and/or complete the Nursery application form.
Children are able to join our nursery the term after they turn 3 for a funded session, or can self-fund once the child has turned 3 but is waiting for funding, depending on our numbers.
Our renovated nursery classroom is inviting and bright and is full of resources to allow your child to explore and learn whilst they make friends. Sessions are taught by our experienced Class Teachers and Nursery Nurse to ensure that your child gets off to the very best start. We offer a total of 52 part time places, split between morning and afternoon sessions.
The morning sessions run from 8.45 till 11.45 and the afternoon sessions from 12.15 until 15.15.
If your child is only eligible for 15 hours of funding, the morning sessions are for those children who are in the school year in which they turn 4 (the year before they start school full time in a reception class) and the afternoon sessions are for those children who have birthdays after September and have more than a year to go before they start school full time.
If your child is already 3, but is waiting for funding, you can self-fund 5 sessions of 3 hours, please contact the school office for an up-to-date cost. You would be required to pay for all 5 sessions per week and that space would be kept for your child, whether they attended or not. They would be offered sessions in the afternoon. However, if they are eligible for 30 hours of funding, it is possible that your child could attend both morning and afternoon sessions. Self-funding sessions can only be offered depending on the number of children who will be offered a funded place. Please note, there is an extra charge of £3 per day to cover staffing during the half-hour period between the morning and afternoon session. This must be paid for on the Arbor parent portal or App. If your child has a school meal this must be booked in advance on Arbor. When we are offering places, six weeks in advance of the start date, we will be able to confirm if a self-funded place is available. Payment for these sessions are payable in advance of the start of the term.
Important change to our Nursery hours that will come into effect from 13 April 2026.
Oxfordshire County Council (OCC) has advised that all settings offering funded early education, funded hours offered must be continuous. To comply with this requirement, our Nursery sessions will be adjusted as follows:
There will be no change to the hours for children accessing 15 funded hours.
Children attending 30 funded hours per week
From 13 April 2026, the new hours will be:
Children who are collected at 14:45 will be brought to the school office and will be ready for collection at that time. If you would like your child to stay until 15:15, this will be booked via Arbor under the Clubs section. We will let you know when the club is live, ready for you to book.
We understand that these changes may affect family routines, and we are committed to supporting you through this transition. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.
If you are interested in your child joining our Nursery, please do make an appointment by contacting our school office on 01235 848 333 to arrange a visit and/or complete the Nursery application form
Core Nursery day: 8:45 – 14:45
30 hours Funded Childcare
Our Nursery Class offers extended hours to eligible parents under the '30 hours' scheme. The scheme is designed to help families where both parents work (even part time). To check your eligibility, follow the link below:
Childcare Tax Service
If your child is eligible they can attend both the morning and afternoon sessions, and they are also able to stay in school for the half-hour lunch break, at a charge of £3.00 per day.
Unfortunately, we are unable to split 30-hours funding between ourselves and another provider.

pageCache.text:
Staff Vacancies
Recruitment Process
Employing the right staff is key to the success of our school. We understand that valuing and developing our staff is the best way to access their full potential. We in return seek staff who are committed, passionate about working with children and have a growth mindset. If this is you, please look out for vacancies which will be advertised on this page.
Ridgeway Education Trust is committed to safeguarding, equality and promoting the welfare of children and expects staff working in all its schools to share this commitment. The successful applicant will be subject to satisfactory enhanced DBS, references and pre-employment safeguarding checks. All Leadership roles will require a Section 128 check. The possession of a criminal record will not necessarily prevent an applicant from obtaining a post. All cases are considered confidentially and according to the nature of the role and information disclosed.
To view our Safeguarding policy, please visit /policies

pageCache.pageTitle: Sutton Courtenay CofE Primary School - Early Years Foundation Stage
pageCache.text:
Early Years Foundation Stage
At Sutton Courtenay Primary school we offer education for children the term after they turn 3 years of age. We currently have two classes; a nursery class (Barn Owls) for our youngest children and a Reception class (Robins) for our 4-5 year olds.
We believe that effective education requires both a relevant curriculum and practitioners who understand and are able to implement the curriculum requirements. We understand that children develop rapidly during the early years – physically, intellectually, emotionally and socially. Our provision supports and extends knowledge, skills, understanding and confidence, and helps them to overcome any disadvantages.
We pride ourselves on ensuring all children feel included, secure and valued. We build positive relationships with parents in order to work effectively with them and their children. We offer children experiences that build on what children already know and can do. We encourage a positive attitude and disposition to learn and aim to prevent early failure.
Our early years curriculum is carefully structured through:
provision for the different starting points from which children develop their learning, building on what they can already do;
relevant and appropriate content that matches the different levels of young children’s needs;
planned and purposeful activity that provides opportunities for teaching and learning, both indoors and outdoors. Opportunities for children to engage in activities planned by adults and also those that they plan or initiate themselves.
‘I played all day today, Daddy!’
We know children do not make a distinction between ‘play’ and ‘work’ and so neither do we as practitioners. Children need time to become engrossed, work in depth and complete activities. We spend a lot of time observing children and assessing their levels of involvement. This enables us respond appropriately to children, informed by our knowledge of how children develop and learn and a clear understanding of possible next steps in their development and learning.
Our EYFS team are all highly trained skilled practitioners, our provision prides itself in all children having a key person who is a qualified teacher with the additional support or Teaching Assistants and Nursery nurses. In addition, we offer Weekly Forest School sessions to children who start in our Reception class. Our Forest School sessions are led by a Level 3 trained Forest School Leader.
Quotes from Ofsted over the years
Children in the Early Years get off to a strong start. Staff set high expectations, then do all they can to help children achieve them. Staff support children to practise and build their knowledge and understanding of numbers effectively. The school’s focus on personal, social and emotional development is highly effective. In Nursery, a strong focus on rhymes and singing helps build confidence and important communication skills.(2023)
The early years is a settled, calm and positive environment for learning. Children play happily together and are secure in the good relationships they have with adults in the setting. Children behave well, listen attentively and respond respectfully to adults and each other. Resources are organised and accessible so that children can select the materials they would like to use, make choices in their learning and follow their interests. (2017)
Reception children make rapid progress because of outstanding teaching .(2012)
They tend to make steady progress in the Nursery and rapid progress in the Reception class. (2012)
Inspirational teaching in the Reception class makes children believe in what can they can learn and accomplish. (2012)
Children in the Early Years Foundation Stage make a good start to their education because the tasks are matched well to their needs. (2010)
Children enjoy school because members of staff are skilled at making them feel safe and happy. (2010)
